chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Manqari (or another) ascribed it, saying: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, from the happiness of a person is the lightness of his two opposites.
He said: And what happiness is in this? The happiness is only in the lightness of his two chewers by glorification (of Allah).

key_terms.عَارِضَانِ: Two opposites (referring to the upper and lower jaws/teeth)
key_terms.مَاضِغَانِ: Two chewers (referring to the jaws used for chewing)

ai.seo_question: What does 'lightness of the two opposites' mean in Shia hadith regarding happiness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'lightness of the two opposites' (jawbones) signifies the physical ease of chewing, which facilitates the continuous recitation of *tasbih*. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on linking bodily comfort and ease (*khafah*) directly to spiritual prosperity, suggesting that physical well-being supports consistent devotion. The narration underscores the practical dimension of *dhikr*, where the absence of physical hindrance allows for uninterrupted remembrance of God.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Yahya al-Ash’ari, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim al-Manqari, or another, who ascribed it, saying: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
Indeed, from an individual’s happiness is the lightness of his two opposites.
He said: There is no happiness in this. The happiness is only in the lightness of his two chewers by (which he can perform) glorification (of Allah).
